mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant deviation from zero during high-rate regimes (p > 0.05 in t-test), or the Fed Funds rate does not stay elevated for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 3% for three consecutive months, the market anticipates a pre-emptive rate hike by the Fed, which elevates risk-free rates and dampens equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: During such inflation spikes, SPX 20-day forward returns are non-negative in over 70% of instances (empirical frequency), or the three-month moving average of Fed Funds remains unchanged when inflation crosses 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly PAYEMS (employment growth) accompanied by a decline in UNRATE (unemployment) suggests a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns within 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 2% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by at least 0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: The correlation between PAYEMS and SPX 5-day returns remains below 0.3 in all labor market strengthening episodes, or UNRATE does not fall while PAYEMS rises in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in GDPC1 (real personal consumption) exceeding 3% for two consecutive months indicates robust demand, prompting market participants to price in higher corporate earnings and expanding equity valuations, which supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly growth > 3% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In late-cycle demand regimes, GDPC1 growth > 3% does not predict SPX 20-day outperformance with a p-value > 0.05 in a two-tailed test.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (industrial production) by more than 2% in a month signals supply-side weakness, prompting investors to seek safety in government bonds and reducing equity demand, which results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by more than 2% in a single month
failure_condition: During confirmed supply shocks, INDPRO drops >2% but SPX 60-day returns show no significant negative deviation from historical averages (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the RSAFS (reserves as a share of GDP) falls below 60% for three consecutive months, it indicates excess liquidity in the banking system, which typically lowers real interest rates and supports equity price appreciation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: RSAFS remains below 60% but SPX 20-day returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a low-unemployment environment where UNRATE remains below 4% for four consecutive months while HOUST (housing starts) remains flat or rising suggests a resilient labor market and stable housing demand, which supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% for four consecutive months and HOUST >= 0 for four consecutive months
failure_condition: In labor-resilient regimes, the joint signal does not predict SPX 60-day outperformance with a Sharpe ratio exceeding 0.5.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in both RSAFS (reserves/GDP) and UNRATE (unemployment) below their 2018 averages for two consecutive months suggests structural supply constraints and weak demand, which compresses equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 2018_avg and UNRATE < 2018_avg for two consecutive months
failure_condition: During such imbalances, SPX 5-day returns show no consistent negative trend (trend test p > 0.05).
